sections.h2: Where is the Moore County Register of Deeds, and when is it open?
sections.html:
The Moore County Register of Deeds is at 26 Courthouse Square in Carthage, NC 28327, and the office is open Monday through Friday from 8 am to 5 pm. The mailing address is P.O. Box 1210, Carthage, NC 28327, and the phone number is 910-947-6370.

The county's office page describes the mission as protecting and preserving the public records and keeping them accurate and open to the public. Marriage licenses are handled by appointment: finish the application first, then call and choose option 1.

The same page carries a notice sellers and researchers should read. The office is back-filling its index for records from January 1, 1888 to June 30, 1988, adding extra parties as it goes, so not every name may show up online for those years. The page advises checking the index books in the office to be sure every party is found.

sections.h2: How do I record a deed in Moore County?
sections.html:
You bring a finished, signed and notarized deed to the Carthage office, or your attorney or title company submits it electronically. Staff cannot prepare the deed or give legal advice, so a lawyer drafts it before it comes in.

The county's recording requirements page lists what the first page must show before a deed or deed of trust prepared in North Carolina will be accepted.

  • The name of the person who drafted the document.
  • A return name and address, plus a self-addressed stamped envelope.
  • The grantee's mailing address, which the Tax Department uses for the new owner's bill.
  • The excise tax stamp on the front of the deed.
  • The type of instrument, written at the top of the first page.

The excise stamp and the filing fee go in together. Moore County's page states the calculation as $2 per $1,000, or $1 for each $500 or fraction of it, of the purchase price. State law puts that payment on the seller, as the transferor (G.S. 105-228.30).

sections.h2: What formatting rules can trigger an extra recording fee in Moore County?
sections.html:
A document that misses the state recording standards is still recorded, but the office adds a $25 non-standard fee on top of the recording fee. The standards come from G.S. 161-14(b) and are repeated on the Moore County page.

Moore County recording standards for ordinary deeds
ItemRequirement
Paper sizeLetter (8.5 by 11 inches) or legal (8.5 by 14 inches)
Top margin, first page3 inches blank
Other marginsHalf an inch on remaining sides of page one and all sides of later pages
TypeBlack on white, no smaller than 9 points
PagesSingle-sided only
Instrument typeStated at the top of page one

The county notes that UCC forms on the national standard form and satisfactions are exempt. The register can also waive the fee for small type when the scanned image is still legible. If the notary's acknowledgment is dated before July 1, 2002, no non-standard fee applies.

sections.h2: Can attorneys and title companies e-record in Moore County?
sections.html:
Yes. The office accepts electronic recording from attorneys, title companies and financial institutions that sign up with an approved vendor. The county lists three: Epen (eRecording Partners), CSC and Simplifile.

The filer then sends the county a completed Memorandum of Understanding by email for approval. A homeowner selling alone does not need to do this, because the closing attorney or title company usually holds the account.

  • Electronic filers need the vendor account and the approved agreement on file before the first submission.
  • Paper filings go to the Carthage counter or to P.O. Box 1210 with a check for the stamp and fee.
  • Either way, the same page-one and margin rules apply.

sections.h2: What do Moore County recording fees and the free alert service cost?
sections.html:
Statewide recording fees apply here: $26.00 for the first 15 pages of a general instrument and $4.00 for each extra page, or $64.00 for the first 35 pages of a deed of trust plus $4.00 for each extra page (G.S. 161-10). Satisfactions of a mortgage or deed of trust are recorded without a fee.

Moore County also runs a free Real Estate Recording Notification Service. After you sign up, the office emails you whenever a document is recorded under a name you list. A single email address can watch up to 10 names or name variations, and the alert covers only documents recorded after sign-up.

For a house owner, that alert is a cheap way to spot a surprise lien or a deed filed in your name that you did not expect. Heirs sorting out a parent's estate can watch both the parent's name and their own.

sections.h2: How big is Moore County, and what does the Census say about its housing?
sections.html:
Moore County had an estimated 110,619 residents on July 1, 2025, up 10.9% from the April 2020 estimates base, according to the Census Bureau. It spans 697.68 square miles of land and counted 142.9 people per square mile in 2020.

Housing figures from the 2020-2024 survey show a county where about three in four households own their homes.

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $351,400.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 76.4%.
  • Median gross rent: $1,254.
  • Residents age 65 and over: 25.4%.
  • Building permits in 2025: 1,077.

With a quarter of residents past 65 and over a thousand building permits in a year, the Carthage office sees both estate transfers and new construction. A clean chain of recorded documents helps a sale go smoothly, especially when the house has changed hands inside a family.

sections.h2: Where does a Moore County seller check the tax side after recording?
sections.html:
Once a deed is recorded, the Land Records Section of the county Tax Department updates ownership using what was filed with the Register of Deeds or the Clerk of Court. The Tax Department page gives the office as 1 Courthouse Square in Carthage, phone 910-947-2255, open 8 am to 5 pm Monday through Friday.

Moore County's most recent revaluation took effect January 1, 2023, and the county schedules the next one for 2027, with a four-year cycle after that unless state law or the market calls for a different schedule. A recorded sale does not by itself reset the assessed value, though the county's FAQ says a sale price far outside the assessment can prompt an appraiser visit.

Ask the Tax Department for the current bill and any past-due balance before closing so the payoff is on the settlement statement.

faqs.q: What are the Moore County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: The office is open Monday through Friday, 8 am to 5 pm, at 26 Courthouse Square in Carthage. Call 910-947-6370 for questions. Marriage licenses are by appointment after the application is completed.

faqs.q: What must be on the first page of a deed recorded in Moore County?
faqs.a: The first page needs the drafter's name, a return name and address with a stamped envelope, the grantee's mailing address, the excise tax stamp, and the instrument type at the top. A blank 3-inch top margin is also required.

faqs.q: How much is the non-standard document fee in Moore County?
faqs.a: It is $25, charged in addition to the recording fee when a document does not meet the state formatting standards. The register may waive it for small type if the scanned image is still legible.

faqs.q: Can I get an email when a document is recorded in my name?
faqs.a: Yes. Moore County offers a free Real Estate Recording Notification Service that emails you when a document is recorded under a name you list. You can monitor up to 10 names per email address, and it covers documents recorded after you sign up.

faqs.q: Which Moore County office handles my property tax bill after the sale?
faqs.a: The county Tax Department in Carthage handles listing, appraisal and collection. Its Land Records Section updates the owner record from recorded deeds, and you can reach the office at 910-947-2255.
